1	# sequence-engine
2	
3	Small sequence model engine with explicit truncated backpropagation, written so that truncation points and hidden-state resets are observable from the public API.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m sequence_engine --selftest
16	
17	The built-in self-check runs only in memory (including the incremental
18	checkpoint path) and writes no files.
19	
20	## Public interface
21	
22	`sequence_engine.Tensor(data)` and `sequence_engine.Sequential(modules)`.
23	- `Tensor.tolist() -> list`, `Tensor.shape -> list[int]`.
24	- `Sequential.forward(batch, hidden=None) -> (output, hidden)`.
25	- `Sequential.backward(loss) -> None` accumulates gradients.
26	  `loss` is a scalar/Tensor seed or the tuple form `(output, upstream)`
27	  carrying the exact Tensor returned by the preceding `forward`.
28	  Calling `backward` without a preceding `forward`, or twice for one
29	  `forward`, raises `RuntimeError`. If a layer raises mid-pass the partial
30	  gradients are rolled back, the layer caches are restored by replaying
31	  the segment's forward, and the same `backward` may be retried; a retry
32	  is not a second backward. If that replay itself cannot rebuild the
33	  caches the rebuild failure is surfaced (not swallowed) as a `ValueError`
34	  naming the rebuild stage, chained onto the original layer exception,
35	  which is still the error handed to the caller -- it is neither masked
36	  nor replaced.
37	- `Sequential.zero_grad() -> None` clears accumulated gradients.
38	- `Sequential.update(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place step
39	  `theta <- theta - learning_rate * grad` on every parameter. Gradients are
40	  not cleared; parameters without a gradient are unchanged. A non-finite or
41	  non-numeric learning rate raises `ValueError`.
42	- `Sequential.adam_step(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place Adam
43	  step with coefficients fixed by the engine (they are not parameters of
44	  the call and the optimizer kind cannot be swapped): moments are updated
45	  as `m <- 0.9*m + 0.1*g` and `v <- 0.999*v + 0.001*g^2`, the step count
46	  `t` starts at 1 on the first call and increments by one each call, and
47	  the parameter update is
48	  `theta <- theta - lr * (m/(1-0.9^t)) / (sqrt(v/(1-0.999^t)) + 1e-8)`.
49	  Parameters without a gradient are unchanged but `t` still advances;
50	  gradients are not cleared. The one-step `update`, gradient accumulation
51	  and `zero_grad` semantics are unchanged and the two optimizer paths do
52	  not share any state besides the parameters. A non-finite or non-numeric
53	  learning rate raises `ValueError`; an unstepped state starts at `t = 0`
54	  with zero moments.
55	- `Sequential.set_recompute(enabled) -> None` switches bounded-memory mode
56	  on or off. With it on, a `forward` keeps only the slice-boundary hidden
57	  state plus a few anchors (the segment input and the incoming hidden
58	  values); the matching `backward` recomputes the activations from those
59	  anchors, so retained activation memory stays bounded by the segment
60	  size instead of growing with the total sequence length. Forward
61	  outputs and parameter gradients are bitwise identical with the switch
62	  on or off. The switch may only be flipped between segments; flipping it
63	  while a backward is pending raises `RuntimeError` without touching the
64	  container. If a parameter is rewritten while a recompute segment is in
65	  flight, `backward` raises `RuntimeError` before any gradient is
66	  accumulated (no half state; the failed pass does not consume the
67	  forward and may be retried on a fresh forward).
68	- `Sequential.parameters() -> list[Tensor]` in registration order.
69	- `Sequential.save(target) -> None` fixes parameters, accumulated gradients
70	  (zeros for parameters that have none), the optimizer state (Adam first
71	  and second moments and step count; zero moments and `t = 0` when
72	  `adam_step` has never run), the slice-boundary hidden state and the
73	  layer order in one versioned binary checkpoint. `target` is a
74	  filesystem path (`str`/`os.PathLike`), an existing directory used as an
75	  incremental checkpoint chain, a `MemoryChain`, or an in-memory
76	  `bytearray`; saving mutates no existing state and repeated saves of the
77	  same state produce identical bytes. A boundary exists before the first
78	  segment and after every `forward` -- the hidden state returned by that
79	  forward *is* the boundary -- so saving is allowed even when the latest
80	  forward has not been back-propagated yet; the snapshot fixes the boundary
81	  state, not the in-flight activations.
82	- `Sequential.load(source) -> hidden | None` restores a checkpoint from a
83	  path, an incremental-chain directory, a `MemoryChain`, or bytes-like
84	  buffer and returns the restored hidden-state list for the next
85	  `forward(batch, hidden)`. The format version (the previous format
86	  versions 1 and 2 are read and migrated item by item; a migrated
87	  optimizer state starts at `t = 0` with zero moments;
88	  `Sequential.loaded_from_version` reports the version a successful load
89	  came from), every tensor shape and the layer order (count, layer
90	  kinds, per-layer parameter shapes) are checked first; hidden-state
91	  shapes are verified on the spot, even for a model that has never run a
92	  forward. Any mismatch, truncation, corruption or missing field rejects
93	  the whole checkpoint with `ValueError` -- nothing is partially applied
94	  or silently filled in. A missing path raises `FileNotFoundError`.
95	- `Sequential.compact(target, up_to=None) -> None` compacts an existing
96	  incremental checkpoint chain (a chain directory or a `MemoryChain`) in
97	  place. Compaction is a streaming online fold: segments are checked one
98	  by one while the new basis is written out, the remaining deltas are
99	  converted a segment at a time in the slots the original chain already
100	  owned, and saves and loads proceed normally throughout -- peak on-disk
101	  usage never exceeds the original chain plus one new basis segment, and
102	  the `head` pointer names at every instant one complete chain (the old
103	  head or the new). The basis segment and the deltas through `up_to` (the
104	  current head when omitted) are folded into one new basis segment and the
105	  remaining deltas are renumbered after it. The reassembled state --
106	  parameters, gradients, optimizer moments and step count, hidden state
107	  -- is bit for bit identical before and after, compaction advances no
108	  optimizer step, and the segment count decreases deterministically by
109	  exactly the merged range. Repeating the same compaction is a no-op, as
110	  is a chain with nothing to merge (basis only, or `up_to=0`).
111	  Old-version segments participate exactly as on load, and the compacted
112	  chain is rewritten in the current format version. A process killed
113	  mid-compaction leaves either the old or the new head reachable -- the
114	  next open of the chain finishes the roll-forward -- so the directory
115	  always holds one complete chain. A missing directory raises
116	  `FileNotFoundError`, an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
117	  `OSError`, and any corrupt, truncated or shape-inconsistent segment
118	  rejects the whole compaction with `ValueError` before anything is
119	  written. Passing a list of chain directories (or `MemoryChain`s)
120	  instead of one chain performs the family-level fold (`up_to` is not
121	  accepted): the prefix segments all members reach through the same
122	  shared files are merged into one new basis segment stored once and
123	  shared by every member, each member's head moves to the new history
124	  and its member-owned tail follows it, and every member's reassembled
125	  state is bit for bit unchanged with no optimizer step advanced. The
126	  family fold is idempotent, leaves a family with no foldable prefix as
127	  it was, and a killed fold leaves every member loadable with the
128	  residue reclaimed by the next family operation. A missing member
129	  directory or referenced segment raises `FileNotFoundError` without
130	  touching the other members; truncated, missing-field or out-of-order
131	  segments or members whose shapes/layer order disagree reject the whole
132	  family fold with `ValueError` (naming the disagreeing shapes and
133	  layer order); an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
134	  `OSError`.
135	- `Sequential.fork(source, target, up_to=None) -> None` derives a branch
136	  chain from an existing incremental checkpoint chain at segment `up_to`
137	  (the source chain's current head when omitted). The branch chain
138	  directory created at `target` shares every segment up to and including
139	  the fork point with the source chain -- the prefix files are
140	  hard-linked, so they are stored once -- and from then on maintains
141	  only its own `head` and the delta segments it appends. The two chains
142	  save, load, compact and verify independently and in parallel: a state
143	  reassembled from either chain is bit for bit identical to the state an
144	  unforked chain would hold, appends landing on the same segment
145	  position in both chains leave each other's bytes untouched, and a
146	  shared segment (immutable by construction) is never observed
147	  half-written. A shared segment's bytes are reclaimed by reachability,
148	  exactly when no chain's head can reach it any more -- whether the
149	  reference went away through a compaction or through the deletion of a
150	  whole branch directory -- and a process killed at any point neither
151	  loses a reachable segment nor leaks an unreachable one; every chain
152	  still standing reopens as one complete state. The fork itself is
153	  atomic: the branch is staged under a private sibling directory and
154	  renamed into place, so `target` either appears as one complete chain
155	  or not at all. A fork point that falls between segment positions (a
156	  non-integer) or names a segment the chain has not committed, and a
157	  `target` that already exists, raise `ValueError`; a missing source
158	  directory or a missing referenced segment raises `FileNotFoundError`;
159	  an unwritable destination or a full disk raises `OSError`. Forking a
160	  `MemoryChain` takes no `target` and returns the new `MemoryChain`.
161	- `Sequential.delete(target) -> None` deletes one branch chain of a
162	  family: the chain directory, its `head` and the incremental segments
163	  it alone owned are removed. A shared segment's bytes are reclaimed by
164	  reachability only -- exactly when no chain's head can reach it any
165	  more -- and are kept byte for byte intact while any chain still
166	  references them. The directory is renamed aside in one atomic step
167	  and then emptied, so a fork or compaction running on the same family
168	  at any moment observes each surviving chain as one complete state,
169	  and a process killed at any point leaves every surviving chain
170	  loadable, with the residue (a detached staging directory, or segments
171	  no head can reach) swept deterministically by the next fork,
172	  compaction or deletion. The sweep is a pure reachability function:
173	  repeating it changes nothing and it advances no chain's optimizer
174	  step count. A `target` that does not exist or was already deleted
175	  raises `FileNotFoundError` and leaves every other chain untouched; a
176	  directory that exists but has no `head`, or holds a chain that cannot
177	  be parsed, raises `ValueError` and removes not a single shared
178	  segment; an unwritable directory or a full disk raises `OSError`, and
179	  an interrupted teardown leaves only whole segment files behind --
180	  never a half-written one. Deleting a `MemoryChain` drops its head
181	  and segments in one critical section, and the emptied chain can be
182	  reused.
183	- `Sequential.merge(source, target) -> None` merges one chain's current
184	  state onto another chain (two chain directories, or two
185	  `MemoryChain` stores). The target keeps every segment it already had
186	  and exactly one new delta segment is appended after its head,
187	  carrying only the tensors in which the source chain's head state
188	  differs from the target's current state (an empty delta when the two
189	  already agree). Loading the target afterwards is bit for bit
190	  identical to loading the source at merge time; the source chain --
191	  its head and its segment files -- is not modified at all, and the two
192	  chains then evolve independently. Segments the family already shares
193	  are never stored twice: the appended segment belongs to the target
194	  alone and holds only the part the source alone owned that genuinely
195	  differs. Repeating the merge of the same state appends another empty
196	  delta and changes nothing, and the number of segments grows exactly
197	  with the difference (always by one segment). The merge advances no
198	  optimizer step: the target inherits the source's complete state, its
199	  step count included, and a full save right afterwards lands exactly
200	  the merged state. A missing source or target directory or a missing
201	  referenced segment raises `FileNotFoundError` and leaves every other
202	  chain untouched; merging a chain into itself, two chains whose
203	  parameter shapes or layer order disagree, or an unparseable chain
204	  structure rejects the whole merge with `ValueError` before one target
205	  byte is rewritten; an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
206	  `OSError`. A process killed mid-merge leaves only the old head or the
207	  new head reachable (both one complete chain), and the residue -- an
208	  orphan segment beyond the old head -- is reclaimed deterministically
209	  by the next fork, compaction, deletion or merge.
210	- `Sequential.verify(source)` verifies an existing incremental checkpoint
211	  chain (a chain directory or a `MemoryChain`) strictly read-only. It
212	  walks the basis and every delta through the `head`, checking each
213	  segment's completeness (framing and CRC), segment order, the basis
214	  reference and every tensor/layer shape, and returns a success report
215	  (`ok`, `head`, `segments`) for an intact chain. A truncated segment,
216	  missing field, out-of-order segment, or a shape/layer-order mismatch
217	  rejects the **whole** chain with `ValueError` whose message names the
218	  first bad segment's position and the reason; the chain directory is not
219	  modified by a single byte (a compaction interrupted on disk is
220	  inspected in place, not rolled forward). A missing chain directory
221	  raises `FileNotFoundError`; an operating-system level read failure
222	  raises `OSError`. `source` may also be a list of chain directories --
223	  a chain family whose members share prefix segments after a fork. Every
224	  member is then verified in turn with the same read-only walk, a sound
225	  family returns a family report (`ok`, `members`, `chains`), and the
226	  first bad segment across the family is reported with its position, the
227	  reason and -- for a shared segment -- every chain whose head reaches
228	  it.
229	- `Sequential.export_family(members, target) -> None` packs a whole
230	  chain family into one self-contained artifact. `members` is the
231	  sequence of the family's chain directories (its order is preserved);
232	  `target` is the artifact file's destination path. Segments the
233	  members share (the hard-linked fork prefix) are stored once as
234	  deduplicated blocks; each member's head and its member-owned tail
235	  segments are preserved exactly, positions included. The export
236	  advances no member's optimizer step and changes no member by a byte,
237	  and exporting the same family twice produces identical artifacts.
238	  Members keep saving, loading and appending while the export runs --
239	  the artifact fixes one consistent, quiescent snapshot and no member
240	  is ever observed as half a chain. A missing member directory or
241	  referenced segment raises `FileNotFoundError`; a truncated, corrupt
242	  or out-of-order segment, or members whose parameter shapes or layer
243	  order disagree, rejects the whole export with `ValueError` before
244	  the artifact is written; an unwritable destination directory or a
245	  full disk raises `OSError`. The artifact file itself is written
246	  through a temp file and atomically renamed, so a process killed
247	  mid-export leaves only the rejected temp file behind. With a
248	  sequence of `MemoryChain` members no `target` is given and the
249	  artifact bytes are returned.
250	- `Sequential.import_family(source, target) -> None` restores a family
251	  artifact into a chain family. `source` is a family artifact file
252	  path; `target` is an existing directory that receives one chain
253	  directory per family member. The artifact is validated in full
254	  before anything is written; each member is staged privately (segment
255	  links first, the head pointer last -- the fork commit order) and
256	  renamed into place atomically, so a member appears as one complete
257	  chain or not at all. The restored member count, segment positions
258	  and shared layout match the exported family, and every member's
259	  parameters, gradients, optimizer state and step count and hidden
260	  state restore bit for bit; no optimizer step advances. A process
261	  killed mid-import leaves a resumable marker plus whole-file staging
262	  debris: re-running the same import finishes the remaining members
263	  with a result bit for bit identical to one uninterrupted run, and
264	  the debris is reclaimed deterministically by the next family
265	  operation over the target directory. If the target already holds a
266	  chain family member the import raises `ValueError` without changing
267	  one byte there. A missing artifact file or target directory raises
268	  `FileNotFoundError`; a torn, truncated, missing-field, reordered or
269	  shape/layer-order-inconsistent artifact rejects the whole import
270	  with `ValueError`; an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
271	  `OSError`. With artifact bytes as `source` (as returned by
272	  `export_family` for `MemoryChain` members) no `target` is given and
273	  a list of `MemoryChain` stores is returned.
274	
275	### Threading
276	
277	All `Sequential` operations are serialised by one per-container lock, so
278	multiple threads may interleave `forward`, `backward`, `update`,
279	`adam_step`, `save` and `load`. Under any interleaving each parameter's
280	final value is one a serial execution of the same calls could have
281	produced: `update` and `adam_step` each apply as one atomic step, a
282	`load` is never observed half-applied, and no `save` can read a
283	half-written tensor (optimizer moments included). Every snapshot
284	corresponds to one complete slice boundary -- never two passes half
285	mixed. When two threads save to the same file path the bytes on disk are
286	always one or the other writer's complete checkpoint (never a blend).
287	
288	## Checkpoint file semantics
289	
290	Path saves are atomic: bytes go to a temporary file in the destination
291	directory, which is `os.replace`d over any existing file (no backup is
292	kept). A process killed mid-write leaves only the rejected temporary file;
293	the final path either holds the previous complete checkpoint or the new
294	one. A half-written or corrupted file at the load path is detected by its
295	trailer and CRC and refused with `ValueError`.
296	
297	Floats are stored as raw IEEE-754 float64 values, so a save/load round-trip
298	is bitwise identical, including the sign of negative zero. Integers must
299	fit in int64 (the Adam step count included) and all serialized numbers
300	must be finite; oversized integers or non-finite floats raise
301	`ValueError` on save -- optimizer moments with such values can never
302	enter a checkpoint -- and a payload that merely contains an oversized or
303	non-finite value is refused on load. Saving into a directory that does
304	not exist or is not writable, or failing because the disk is full,
305	raises `OSError`; the caller chooses the destination path.
306	
307	## Checkpoint format versions
308	
309	The on-disk format is versioned. This build writes **version 3** and
310	still reads **versions 1 and 2**: an old file is migrated item by item
311	into the current document shape and the source version is recorded; if
312	migration fails on any item the whole file is rejected rather than
313	silently filled in. Version 3 adds the optimizer state (Adam first/second
314	moments and step count); a version-1 or version-2 checkpoint has no such
315	state and migrates to `t = 0` with zero moments. A file with an unknown
316	version, or a header with a field added or removed, is rejected with
317	`ValueError`. A migrated state re-saves as native version 3. Unknown
318	(future) versions are never guessed; they are refused.
319	
320	## Incremental checkpoint chains
321	
322	Passing an existing directory (or a `MemoryChain`) to `save`/`load` uses an
323	incremental chain instead of one self-contained file:
324	
325	- the first save writes a full **basis** segment (`seg-0000000000.seqd`);
326	- every later save appends a delta segment naming only the tensors that
327	  changed, compared by encoded leaf identity (so float sign bits such as
328	  `-0.0` count); unchanged saves append an empty delta deterministically,
329	  and layers with no parameters participate like any other layer;
330	- a `head` pointer names the newest committed segment. Each segment file is
331	  written completely and atomically before the head is advanced, so a crash,
332	  a full disk or two saves racing into one directory always leave a single
333	  complete chain reachable from `head`. A training process killed at any
334	  point therefore leaves a chain that loads to exactly the last complete
335	  commit, and continuing from it -- appending deltas or taking full saves
336	  -- stays bit for bit identical to the uninterrupted run.
337	
338	`Sequential.compact` (or `checkpoint.compact_chain`) folds the basis and a
339	prefix of the deltas into one new basis segment in place as a streaming
340	online compaction; see its entry in the interface list above. The fold
341	walks and checks segments as it writes the new basis, converts the tail a
342	segment at a time in the slots the chain already owned, and commits
343	through a stage-then-publish protocol guarded by a cross-process directory
344	lock and lease: concurrent saves, loads, verifies and compactions on one
345	directory are serialised at each step (a live fold is read straight
346	through rather than waited on), a compaction killed at any point is
347	completed by the next open, and `head` always points at one complete
348	chain. Peak disk usage stays within the original chain plus the single
349	new basis segment.
350	
351	A whole chain family is compacted in one call too: `Sequential.compact`
352	(or `checkpoint.compact_family`) takes the sequence of member chain
353	directories and folds the prefix segments every member reaches through
354	the same shared files (the hard-linked fork prefix) into one new basis
355	segment stored once and shared by every member. Each member's head is
356	advanced to that new history while the tail segments it alone owned
357	follow the new basis in their original order, so the state every member
358	reassembles -- parameters, gradients, optimizer state and hidden state
359	-- is bit for bit unchanged and no member's optimizer step moves. The
360	segment count drops deterministically by exactly the folded range,
361	repeating the same family fold is a no-op, and a family with no
362	foldable prefix is left as it was. Each member runs the same streaming,
363	crash-safe fold a single-chain compaction uses (saves, loads and
364	incremental appends keep flowing and no member is ever observed as half
365	a chain); the family fold is serialised against single-chain
366	compactions, forks, merges and deletions by the directory locks and
367	leases. Hard-killed mid-fold, each member still loads one complete
368	state -- its own interrupted fold rolls forward on the next open -- and
369	the next family operation finishes the fold and reclaims the residue,
370	neither deleting a reachable shared segment nor leaking an unreachable
371	one. `checkpoint.compact_family_memory` provides the same family fold for
372	`MemoryChain` stores.
373	
374	`Sequential.fork` (or `checkpoint.fork_chain`) turns one chain into a
375	chain family: the branch directory shares the segments up to the fork
376	point with the source chain (hard links, so the prefix is stored once)
377	and then grows its own tail under its own `head`. Every chain of the
378	family saves, loads, compacts and verifies independently; a shared
379	segment's bytes are reclaimed exactly when no chain's head can reach it
380	any more. `Sequential.delete` (or `checkpoint.delete_chain`) removes one
381	branch of the family -- its directory, its head and the segments it
382	alone owned -- atomically with respect to concurrent forks and
383	compactions, and deterministically sweeps crash residue (staging
384	directories of killed forks/deletes, segments no head can reach) on
385	every fork, compaction, deletion and merge. `Sequential.merge` (or
386	`checkpoint.merge_chains`) lands one chain's current state onto another
387	inside the family: the target keeps all of its segments and gains one
388	target-owned delta carrying only the genuine difference from the
389	source, so the target then loads to the source's state bit for bit
390	while the source is untouched and the shared prefix is stored once;
391	the merge uses the same segment-then-head append commit a save does,
392	so a kill leaves only the old or the new head and its orphan residue
393	is swept on the next family operation. `checkpoint.verify_chain` (or
394	`Sequential.verify`) accepts a list of chain directories to verify a
395	whole family read-only, reporting the first bad segment with every chain
396	that reaches it.
397	
398	`checkpoint.export_family` (or `Sequential.export_family`) packs a whole
399	chain family into one self-contained artifact file (magic `SEQFAMX1`):
400	every distinct shared segment file becomes one deduplicated block and a
401	manifest records the member order, each member's head and the block
402	filling each of its segment positions, so the artifact stores the shared
403	history once and is a deterministic pure function of the family.
404	`checkpoint.import_family` (or `Sequential.import_family`) restores the
405	artifact into chain directories with the same member count, segment
406	positions, hard-link sharing layout and bit-for-bit state; each member
407	is staged privately and renamed into place atomically, a killed import
408	is resumed by re-running it (the result is bit for bit identical to one
409	uninterrupted run), and its staging debris is reclaimed by the next
410	family operation over the target directory. Neither direction advances
411	any member's optimizer step, both serialise with forks, merges,
412	deletions and single-chain/family compactions through the directory
413	locks and leases, and family verification covers the restored members
414	read-only in one call. `checkpoint.export_family_memory` /
415	`checkpoint.import_family_memory` provide the same pack/restore for
416	`MemoryChain` families, with reference-shared segments becoming one
417	shared object again.
418	
419	Loading walks the basis and every delta up to the head and reassembles the
420	state by layer (parameters, gradients, optimizer moments and step count,
421	then hidden slots). The reassembled state is bit for bit identical to
422	the full snapshot taken at the same moment, including a chain written by
423	the previous version-2 engine: old deltas are read, their hidden indices
424	remapped, and the missing optimizer state filled in from the starting
425	values. Any segment in the chain that is truncated, corrupt, missing a
426	field, out of order, changes the layer order or parameter/shapes, or
427	introduces hidden state incompletely makes the load reject the **whole**
428	chain with `ValueError`. A missing chain directory or a referenced
429	segment file that is absent raises `FileNotFoundError`; an unwritable
430	directory or a full disk raises `OSError`. A chain cannot change the
431	model's layer order or parameter shapes -- use a fresh full snapshot for
432	a different model.
433	
434	`MemoryChain` (exported from `sequence_engine`) is an in-memory chain with
435	identical commit semantics, useful for tests and long-running processes that
436	want incremental snapshots without files.
437	
438	## Tests
439	
440	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
441	
442	## Limits
443	
444	CPU only; no GPU backend.
445	One backward pass per forward pass.
446	The engine trains nothing on its own and ships no dataset.
447

# sequence-engine

Small sequence model engine with explicit truncated backpropagation, written so that truncation points and hidden-state resets are observable from the public API.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m sequence_engine --selftest

The built-in self-check runs only in memory (including the incremental
checkpoint path) and writes no files.

## Public interface

`sequence_engine.Tensor(data)` and `sequence_engine.Sequential(modules)`.
- `Tensor.tolist() -> list`, `Tensor.shape -> list[int]`.
- `Sequential.forward(batch, hidden=None) -> (output, hidden)`.
- `Sequential.backward(loss) -> None` accumulates gradients.
  `loss` is a scalar/Tensor seed or the tuple form `(output, upstream)`
  carrying the exact Tensor returned by the preceding `forward`.
  Calling `backward` without a preceding `forward`, or twice for one
  `forward`, raises `RuntimeError`. If a layer raises mid-pass the partial
  gradients are rolled back, the layer caches are restored by replaying
  the segment's forward, and the same `backward` may be retried; a retry
  is not a second backward. If that replay itself cannot rebuild the
  caches the rebuild failure is surfaced (not swallowed) as a `ValueError`
  naming the rebuild stage, chained onto the original layer exception,
  which is still the error handed to the caller -- it is neither masked
  nor replaced.
- `Sequential.zero_grad() -> None` clears accumulated gradients.
- `Sequential.update(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place step
  `theta <- theta - learning_rate * grad` on every parameter. Gradients are
  not cleared; parameters without a gradient are unchanged. A non-finite or
  non-numeric learning rate raises `ValueError`.
- `Sequential.adam_step(learning_rate) -> None` performs one in-place Adam
  step with coefficients fixed by the engine (they are not parameters of
  the call and the optimizer kind cannot be swapped): moments are updated
  as `m <- 0.9*m + 0.1*g` and `v <- 0.999*v + 0.001*g^2`, the step count
  `t` starts at 1 on the first call and increments by one each call, and
  the parameter update is
  `theta <- theta - lr * (m/(1-0.9^t)) / (sqrt(v/(1-0.999^t)) + 1e-8)`.
  Parameters without a gradient are unchanged but `t` still advances;
  gradients are not cleared. The one-step `update`, gradient accumulation
  and `zero_grad` semantics are unchanged and the two optimizer paths do
  not share any state besides the parameters. A non-finite or non-numeric
  learning rate raises `ValueError`; an unstepped state starts at `t = 0`
  with zero moments.
- `Sequential.set_recompute(enabled) -> None` switches bounded-memory mode
  on or off. With it on, a `forward` keeps only the slice-boundary hidden
  state plus a few anchors (the segment input and the incoming hidden
  values); the matching `backward` recomputes the activations from those
  anchors, so retained activation memory stays bounded by the segment
  size instead of growing with the total sequence length. Forward
  outputs and parameter gradients are bitwise identical with the switch
  on or off. The switch may only be flipped between segments; flipping it
  while a backward is pending raises `RuntimeError` without touching the
  container. If a parameter is rewritten while a recompute segment is in
  flight, `backward` raises `RuntimeError` before any gradient is
  accumulated (no half state; the failed pass does not consume the
  forward and may be retried on a fresh forward).
- `Sequential.parameters() -> list[Tensor]` in registration order.
- `Sequential.save(target) -> None` fixes parameters, accumulated gradients
  (zeros for parameters that have none), the optimizer state (Adam first
  and second moments and step count; zero moments and `t = 0` when
  `adam_step` has never run), the slice-boundary hidden state and the
  layer order in one versioned binary checkpoint. `target` is a
  filesystem path (`str`/`os.PathLike`), an existing directory used as an
  incremental checkpoint chain, a `MemoryChain`, or an in-memory
  `bytearray`; saving mutates no existing state and repeated saves of the
  same state produce identical bytes. A boundary exists before the first
  segment and after every `forward` -- the hidden state returned by that
  forward *is* the boundary -- so saving is allowed even when the latest
  forward has not been back-propagated yet; the snapshot fixes the boundary
  state, not the in-flight activations.
- `Sequential.load(source) -> hidden | None` restores a checkpoint from a
  path, an incremental-chain directory, a `MemoryChain`, or bytes-like
  buffer and returns the restored hidden-state list for the next
  `forward(batch, hidden)`. The format version (the previous format
  versions 1 and 2 are read and migrated item by item; a migrated
  optimizer state starts at `t = 0` with zero moments;
  `Sequential.loaded_from_version` reports the version a successful load
  came from), every tensor shape and the layer order (count, layer
  kinds, per-layer parameter shapes) are checked first; hidden-state
  shapes are verified on the spot, even for a model that has never run a
  forward. Any mismatch, truncation, corruption or missing field rejects
  the whole checkpoint with `ValueError` -- nothing is partially applied
  or silently filled in. A missing path raises `FileNotFoundError`.
- `Sequential.compact(target, up_to=None) -> None` compacts an existing
  incremental checkpoint chain (a chain directory or a `MemoryChain`) in
  place. Compaction is a streaming online fold: segments are checked one
  by one while the new basis is written out, the remaining deltas are
  converted a segment at a time in the slots the original chain already
  owned, and saves and loads proceed normally throughout -- peak on-disk
  usage never exceeds the original chain plus one new basis segment, and
  the `head` pointer names at every instant one complete chain (the old
  head or the new). The basis segment and the deltas through `up_to` (the
  current head when omitted) are folded into one new basis segment and the
  remaining deltas are renumbered after it. The reassembled state --
  parameters, gradients, optimizer moments and step count, hidden state
  -- is bit for bit identical before and after, compaction advances no
  optimizer step, and the segment count decreases deterministically by
  exactly the merged range. Repeating the same compaction is a no-op, as
  is a chain with nothing to merge (basis only, or `up_to=0`).
  Old-version segments participate exactly as on load, and the compacted
  chain is rewritten in the current format version. A process killed
  mid-compaction leaves either the old or the new head reachable -- the
  next open of the chain finishes the roll-forward -- so the directory
  always holds one complete chain. A missing directory raises
  `FileNotFoundError`, an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
  `OSError`, and any corrupt, truncated or shape-inconsistent segment
  rejects the whole compaction with `ValueError` before anything is
  written. Passing a list of chain directories (or `MemoryChain`s)
  instead of one chain performs the family-level fold (`up_to` is not
  accepted): the prefix segments all members reach through the same
  shared files are merged into one new basis segment stored once and
  shared by every member, each member's head moves to the new history
  and its member-owned tail follows it, and every member's reassembled
  state is bit for bit unchanged with no optimizer step advanced. The
  family fold is idempotent, leaves a family with no foldable prefix as
  it was, and a killed fold leaves every member loadable with the
  residue reclaimed by the next family operation. A missing member
  directory or referenced segment raises `FileNotFoundError` without
  touching the other members; truncated, missing-field or out-of-order
  segments or members whose shapes/layer order disagree reject the whole
  family fold with `ValueError` (naming the disagreeing shapes and
  layer order); an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
  `OSError`.
- `Sequential.fork(source, target, up_to=None) -> None` derives a branch
  chain from an existing incremental checkpoint chain at segment `up_to`
  (the source chain's current head when omitted). The branch chain
  directory created at `target` shares every segment up to and including
  the fork point with the source chain -- the prefix files are
  hard-linked, so they are stored once -- and from then on maintains
  only its own `head` and the delta segments it appends. The two chains
  save, load, compact and verify independently and in parallel: a state
  reassembled from either chain is bit for bit identical to the state an
  unforked chain would hold, appends landing on the same segment
  position in both chains leave each other's bytes untouched, and a
  shared segment (immutable by construction) is never observed
  half-written. A shared segment's bytes are reclaimed by reachability,
  exactly when no chain's head can reach it any more -- whether the
  reference went away through a compaction or through the deletion of a
  whole branch directory -- and a process killed at any point neither
  loses a reachable segment nor leaks an unreachable one; every chain
  still standing reopens as one complete state. The fork itself is
  atomic: the branch is staged under a private sibling directory and
  renamed into place, so `target` either appears as one complete chain
  or not at all. A fork point that falls between segment positions (a
  non-integer) or names a segment the chain has not committed, and a
  `target` that already exists, raise `ValueError`; a missing source
  directory or a missing referenced segment raises `FileNotFoundError`;
  an unwritable destination or a full disk raises `OSError`. Forking a
  `MemoryChain` takes no `target` and returns the new `MemoryChain`.
- `Sequential.delete(target) -> None` deletes one branch chain of a
  family: the chain directory, its `head` and the incremental segments
  it alone owned are removed. A shared segment's bytes are reclaimed by
  reachability only -- exactly when no chain's head can reach it any
  more -- and are kept byte for byte intact while any chain still
  references them. The directory is renamed aside in one atomic step
  and then emptied, so a fork or compaction running on the same family
  at any moment observes each surviving chain as one complete state,
  and a process killed at any point leaves every surviving chain
  loadable, with the residue (a detached staging directory, or segments
  no head can reach) swept deterministically by the next fork,
  compaction or deletion. The sweep is a pure reachability function:
  repeating it changes nothing and it advances no chain's optimizer
  step count. A `target` that does not exist or was already deleted
  raises `FileNotFoundError` and leaves every other chain untouched; a
  directory that exists but has no `head`, or holds a chain that cannot
  be parsed, raises `ValueError` and removes not a single shared
  segment; an unwritable directory or a full disk raises `OSError`, and
  an interrupted teardown leaves only whole segment files behind --
  never a half-written one. Deleting a `MemoryChain` drops its head
  and segments in one critical section, and the emptied chain can be
  reused.
- `Sequential.merge(source, target) -> None` merges one chain's current
  state onto another chain (two chain directories, or two
  `MemoryChain` stores). The target keeps every segment it already had
  and exactly one new delta segment is appended after its head,
  carrying only the tensors in which the source chain's head state
  differs from the target's current state (an empty delta when the two
  already agree). Loading the target afterwards is bit for bit
  identical to loading the source at merge time; the source chain --
  its head and its segment files -- is not modified at all, and the two
  chains then evolve independently. Segments the family already shares
  are never stored twice: the appended segment belongs to the target
  alone and holds only the part the source alone owned that genuinely
  differs. Repeating the merge of the same state appends another empty
  delta and changes nothing, and the number of segments grows exactly
  with the difference (always by one segment). The merge advances no
  optimizer step: the target inherits the source's complete state, its
  step count included, and a full save right afterwards lands exactly
  the merged state. A missing source or target directory or a missing
  referenced segment raises `FileNotFoundError` and leaves every other
  chain untouched; merging a chain into itself, two chains whose
  parameter shapes or layer order disagree, or an unparseable chain
  structure rejects the whole merge with `ValueError` before one target
  byte is rewritten; an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
  `OSError`. A process killed mid-merge leaves only the old head or the
  new head reachable (both one complete chain), and the residue -- an
  orphan segment beyond the old head -- is reclaimed deterministically
  by the next fork, compaction, deletion or merge.
- `Sequential.verify(source)` verifies an existing incremental checkpoint
  chain (a chain directory or a `MemoryChain`) strictly read-only. It
  walks the basis and every delta through the `head`, checking each
  segment's completeness (framing and CRC), segment order, the basis
  reference and every tensor/layer shape, and returns a success report
  (`ok`, `head`, `segments`) for an intact chain. A truncated segment,
  missing field, out-of-order segment, or a shape/layer-order mismatch
  rejects the **whole** chain with `ValueError` whose message names the
  first bad segment's position and the reason; the chain directory is not
  modified by a single byte (a compaction interrupted on disk is
  inspected in place, not rolled forward). A missing chain directory
  raises `FileNotFoundError`; an operating-system level read failure
  raises `OSError`. `source` may also be a list of chain directories --
  a chain family whose members share prefix segments after a fork. Every
  member is then verified in turn with the same read-only walk, a sound
  family returns a family report (`ok`, `members`, `chains`), and the
  first bad segment across the family is reported with its position, the
  reason and -- for a shared segment -- every chain whose head reaches
  it.
- `Sequential.export_family(members, target) -> None` packs a whole
  chain family into one self-contained artifact. `members` is the
  sequence of the family's chain directories (its order is preserved);
  `target` is the artifact file's destination path. Segments the
  members share (the hard-linked fork prefix) are stored once as
  deduplicated blocks; each member's head and its member-owned tail
  segments are preserved exactly, positions included. The export
  advances no member's optimizer step and changes no member by a byte,
  and exporting the same family twice produces identical artifacts.
  Members keep saving, loading and appending while the export runs --
  the artifact fixes one consistent, quiescent snapshot and no member
  is ever observed as half a chain. A missing member directory or
  referenced segment raises `FileNotFoundError`; a truncated, corrupt
  or out-of-order segment, or members whose parameter shapes or layer
  order disagree, rejects the whole export with `ValueError` before
  the artifact is written; an unwritable destination directory or a
  full disk raises `OSError`. The artifact file itself is written
  through a temp file and atomically renamed, so a process killed
  mid-export leaves only the rejected temp file behind. With a
  sequence of `MemoryChain` members no `target` is given and the
  artifact bytes are returned.
- `Sequential.import_family(source, target) -> None` restores a family
  artifact into a chain family. `source` is a family artifact file
  path; `target` is an existing directory that receives one chain
  directory per family member. The artifact is validated in full
  before anything is written; each member is staged privately (segment
  links first, the head pointer last -- the fork commit order) and
  renamed into place atomically, so a member appears as one complete
  chain or not at all. The restored member count, segment positions
  and shared layout match the exported family, and every member's
  parameters, gradients, optimizer state and step count and hidden
  state restore bit for bit; no optimizer step advances. A process
  killed mid-import leaves a resumable marker plus whole-file staging
  debris: re-running the same import finishes the remaining members
  with a result bit for bit identical to one uninterrupted run, and
  the debris is reclaimed deterministically by the next family
  operation over the target directory. If the target already holds a
  chain family member the import raises `ValueError` without changing
  one byte there. A missing artifact file or target directory raises
  `FileNotFoundError`; a torn, truncated, missing-field, reordered or
  shape/layer-order-inconsistent artifact rejects the whole import
  with `ValueError`; an unwritable directory or a full disk raises
  `OSError`. With artifact bytes as `source` (as returned by
  `export_family` for `MemoryChain` members) no `target` is given and
  a list of `MemoryChain` stores is returned.

### Threading

All `Sequential` operations are serialised by one per-container lock, so
multiple threads may interleave `forward`, `backward`, `update`,
`adam_step`, `save` and `load`. Under any interleaving each parameter's
final value is one a serial execution of the same calls could have
produced: `update` and `adam_step` each apply as one atomic step, a
`load` is never observed half-applied, and no `save` can read a
half-written tensor (optimizer moments included). Every snapshot
corresponds to one complete slice boundary -- never two passes half
mixed. When two threads save to the same file path the bytes on disk are
always one or the other writer's complete checkpoint (never a blend).

## Checkpoint file semantics

Path saves are atomic: bytes go to a temporary file in the destination
directory, which is `os.replace`d over any existing file (no backup is
kept). A process killed mid-write leaves only the rejected temporary file;
the final path either holds the previous complete checkpoint or the new
one. A half-written or corrupted file at the load path is detected by its
trailer and CRC and refused with `ValueError`.

Floats are stored as raw IEEE-754 float64 values, so a save/load round-trip
is bitwise identical, including the sign of negative zero. Integers must
fit in int64 (the Adam step count included) and all serialized numbers
must be finite; oversized integers or non-finite floats raise
`ValueError` on save -- optimizer moments with such values can never
enter a checkpoint -- and a payload that merely contains an oversized or
non-finite value is refused on load. Saving into a directory that does
not exist or is not writable, or failing because the disk is full,
raises `OSError`; the caller chooses the destination path.

## Checkpoint format versions

The on-disk format is versioned. This build writes **version 3** and
still reads **versions 1 and 2**: an old file is migrated item by item
into the current document shape and the source version is recorded; if
migration fails on any item the whole file is rejected rather than
silently filled in. Version 3 adds the optimizer state (Adam first/second
moments and step count); a version-1 or version-2 checkpoint has no such
state and migrates to `t = 0` with zero moments. A file with an unknown
version, or a header with a field added or removed, is rejected with
`ValueError`. A migrated state re-saves as native version 3. Unknown
(future) versions are never guessed; they are refused.

## Incremental checkpoint chains

Passing an existing directory (or a `MemoryChain`) to `save`/`load` uses an
incremental chain instead of one self-contained file:

- the first save writes a full **basis** segment (`seg-0000000000.seqd`);
- every later save appends a delta segment naming only the tensors that
  changed, compared by encoded leaf identity (so float sign bits such as
  `-0.0` count); unchanged saves append an empty delta deterministically,
  and layers with no parameters participate like any other layer;
- a `head` pointer names the newest committed segment. Each segment file is
  written completely and atomically before the head is advanced, so a crash,
  a full disk or two saves racing into one directory always leave a single
  complete chain reachable from `head`. A training process killed at any
  point therefore leaves a chain that loads to exactly the last complete
  commit, and continuing from it -- appending deltas or taking full saves
  -- stays bit for bit identical to the uninterrupted run.

`Sequential.compact` (or `checkpoint.compact_chain`) folds the basis and a
prefix of the deltas into one new basis segment in place as a streaming
online compaction; see its entry in the interface list above. The fold
walks and checks segments as it writes the new basis, converts the tail a
segment at a time in the slots the chain already owned, and commits
through a stage-then-publish protocol guarded by a cross-process directory
lock and lease: concurrent saves, loads, verifies and compactions on one
directory are serialised at each step (a live fold is read straight
through rather than waited on), a compaction killed at any point is
completed by the next open, and `head` always points at one complete
chain. Peak disk usage stays within the original chain plus the single
new basis segment.

A whole chain family is compacted in one call too: `Sequential.compact`
(or `checkpoint.compact_family`) takes the sequence of member chain
directories and folds the prefix segments every member reaches through
the same shared files (the hard-linked fork prefix) into one new basis
segment stored once and shared by every member. Each member's head is
advanced to that new history while the tail segments it alone owned
follow the new basis in their original order, so the state every member
reassembles -- parameters, gradients, optimizer state and hidden state
-- is bit for bit unchanged and no member's optimizer step moves. The
segment count drops deterministically by exactly the folded range,
repeating the same family fold is a no-op, and a family with no
foldable prefix is left as it was. Each member runs the same streaming,
crash-safe fold a single-chain compaction uses (saves, loads and
incremental appends keep flowing and no member is ever observed as half
a chain); the family fold is serialised against single-chain
compactions, forks, merges and deletions by the directory locks and
leases. Hard-killed mid-fold, each member still loads one complete
state -- its own interrupted fold rolls forward on the next open -- and
the next family operation finishes the fold and reclaims the residue,
neither deleting a reachable shared segment nor leaking an unreachable
one. `checkpoint.compact_family_memory` provides the same family fold for
`MemoryChain` stores.

`Sequential.fork` (or `checkpoint.fork_chain`) turns one chain into a
chain family: the branch directory shares the segments up to the fork
point with the source chain (hard links, so the prefix is stored once)
and then grows its own tail under its own `head`. Every chain of the
family saves, loads, compacts and verifies independently; a shared
segment's bytes are reclaimed exactly when no chain's head can reach it
any more. `Sequential.delete` (or `checkpoint.delete_chain`) removes one
branch of the family -- its directory, its head and the segments it
alone owned -- atomically with respect to concurrent forks and
compactions, and deterministically sweeps crash residue (staging
directories of killed forks/deletes, segments no head can reach) on
every fork, compaction, deletion and merge. `Sequential.merge` (or
`checkpoint.merge_chains`) lands one chain's current state onto another
inside the family: the target keeps all of its segments and gains one
target-owned delta carrying only the genuine difference from the
source, so the target then loads to the source's state bit for bit
while the source is untouched and the shared prefix is stored once;
the merge uses the same segment-then-head append commit a save does,
so a kill leaves only the old or the new head and its orphan residue
is swept on the next family operation. `checkpoint.verify_chain` (or
`Sequential.verify`) accepts a list of chain directories to verify a
whole family read-only, reporting the first bad segment with every chain
that reaches it.

`checkpoint.export_family` (or `Sequential.export_family`) packs a whole
chain family into one self-contained artifact file (magic `SEQFAMX1`):
every distinct shared segment file becomes one deduplicated block and a
manifest records the member order, each member's head and the block
filling each of its segment positions, so the artifact stores the shared
history once and is a deterministic pure function of the family.
`checkpoint.import_family` (or `Sequential.import_family`) restores the
artifact into chain directories with the same member count, segment
positions, hard-link sharing layout and bit-for-bit state; each member
is staged privately and renamed into place atomically, a killed import
is resumed by re-running it (the result is bit for bit identical to one
uninterrupted run), and its staging debris is reclaimed by the next
family operation over the target directory. Neither direction advances
any member's optimizer step, both serialise with forks, merges,
deletions and single-chain/family compactions through the directory
locks and leases, and family verification covers the restored members
read-only in one call. `checkpoint.export_family_memory` /
`checkpoint.import_family_memory` provide the same pack/restore for
`MemoryChain` families, with reference-shared segments becoming one
shared object again.

Loading walks the basis and every delta up to the head and reassembles the
state by layer (parameters, gradients, optimizer moments and step count,
then hidden slots). The reassembled state is bit for bit identical to
the full snapshot taken at the same moment, including a chain written by
the previous version-2 engine: old deltas are read, their hidden indices
remapped, and the missing optimizer state filled in from the starting
values. Any segment in the chain that is truncated, corrupt, missing a
field, out of order, changes the layer order or parameter/shapes, or
introduces hidden state incompletely makes the load reject the **whole**
chain with `ValueError`. A missing chain directory or a referenced
segment file that is absent raises `FileNotFoundError`; an unwritable
directory or a full disk raises `OSError`. A chain cannot change the
model's layer order or parameter shapes -- use a fresh full snapshot for
a different model.

`MemoryChain` (exported from `sequence_engine`) is an in-memory chain with
identical commit semantics, useful for tests and long-running processes that
want incremental snapshots without files.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

CPU only; no GPU backend.
One backward pass per forward pass.
The engine trains nothing on its own and ships no dataset.

Public interface (see README.md):

- ``Tensor(data)`` with ``tolist()`` and ``shape``.
- ``Sequential(modules)`` with ``forward``, ``backward``, ``zero_grad``,
  ``parameters``, ``update`` (one in-place gradient step), ``adam_step``
  (one in-place Adam step with fixed coefficients), ``set_recompute``
  (bounded-memory activation recomputation), ``save`` / ``load``
  (versioned atomic checkpoints to a path, a chain directory, a
  ``MemoryChain`` or a bytearray), ``compact`` (streaming in-place,
  crash-safe compaction of one incremental checkpoint chain, or a single
  family-wide fold over a list of member chains), ``fork``
  (deriving a branch chain that shares the source chain's prefix
  segments and then evolves independently), ``delete`` (removing a
  branch chain and deterministically reclaiming the segments no
  remaining chain can reach), ``merge`` (landing one chain's current
  state onto another by appending one target-owned delta segment),
  ``verify`` (strictly read-only verification of an incremental chain
  or a chain family) and ``export_family`` / ``import_family``
  (packing a whole chain family into one self-contained artifact --
  shared segments stored once -- and restoring it with the same
  members, segment positions, shared layout and bit-for-bit state).
"""

from .checkpoint import MemoryChain
from .sequential import Sequential
from .tensor import Tensor

__all__ = ["Tensor", "Sequential", "MemoryChain"]

1	"""Checkpoint container: versioned binary snapshots for Sequential state.
2	
3	A full snapshot fixes, in one self-describing document:
4	
5	* every parameter tensor,
6	* every accumulated gradient (zeros when a parameter has none yet),
7	* the optimizer state (first and second moment per parameter plus the
8	  step count; zeros and ``t = 0`` when ``adam_step`` has never run),
9	* the slice-boundary hidden state of the latest boundary,
10	* the layer order and per-layer parameter shapes,
11	* the format version.
12	
13	Two on-disk shapes share the same leaf encoding and trailer:
14	
15	* **Full snapshots** (magic ``SEQECKP1``) -- one self-contained file, the
16	  format produced for file paths and in-memory buffers.
17	* **Incremental chains** -- a directory holding one full *basis* segment
18	  (``seg-00000000.seqd``) followed by delta segments that only encode the
19	  tensors that changed.  A small ``head`` pointer names the newest
20	  committed segment, so a crash between the segment write and the pointer
21	  update always recovers the previous complete state.  A chain can be
22	  **compacted** in place by a streaming online fold: the new basis is
23	  checked and written segment by segment, the tail deltas are converted a
24	  segment at a time in slots the chain already owned (so peak disk usage
25	  stays within the original chain plus the one new basis), and saves and
26	  loads interleave the whole time.  A marker plus a cross-process lease
27	  name a fold in progress, with the tail promoted and the head advanced
28	  in one final step, so a crash mid-compaction is rolled forward on the
29	  next open and the directory always holds exactly one complete chain --
30	  the old head's or the new head's.  A chain directory can also be
31	  **verified** strictly read-only: each segment is walked like a load and
32	  the first bad one is located and reported without a single write.
33	* **Chain families** -- a chain can be **forked** at any committed
34	  segment: the new chain directory shares every segment up to and
35	  including the fork point with the source chain (the prefix files are
36	  hard-linked, so they are stored once) and from then on maintains only
37	  its own head and the deltas it appends.  The chains of a family save,
38	  load, stream-compact and verify independently; shared segments are
39	  immutable (every write anywhere is a temp file plus a rename), and a
40	  shared segment's bytes are reclaimed by reachability -- exactly when no
41	  chain's head can reach it any more, whether the reference went away
42	  through a compaction or through the **deletion** of a whole branch.
43	  Reclamation is a pure reachability function, so sweeping again changes
44	  nothing; segments no head can reach (orphans left by a hard kill) and
45	  staging directories from a killed fork, delete or compaction are swept
46	  deterministically on the next fork, compaction, deletion or merge.  A
47	  family of chains can also be compacted in one call --
48	  :func:`compact_family` folds the prefix segments every member reaches
49	  through the same underlying files into one new basis segment shared by
50	  every member, with each member's own tail following it -- and verified
51	  read-only, with the first bad segment reported together with every
52	  chain that reaches it.
53	* **Branch merges** -- one chain's current state can be merged onto
54	  another: the target keeps every segment it had and receives one new,
55	  target-owned delta segment after its head carrying only the tensors in
56	  which the source's head state genuinely differs (an empty delta when
57	  the states already agree), so loading the target is bit for bit the
58	  source's merge-time state while the source's head and files never move
59	  and shared segments are never written twice.  The merge uses the same
60	  segment-then-head append commit a save does -- a kill leaves only the
61	  old or the new head, both one complete chain -- and its orphan residue
62	  is reclaimed by the next fork, compaction, deletion or merge.
63	* **Family export / import** -- a whole chain family packs into one
64	  self-contained artifact file (magic ``SEQFAMX1``): every shared
65	  segment is stored once as a deduplicated block and a manifest records
66	  the member order, each member's head and the block filling each of
67	  its segment positions.  Import restores the artifact into chain
68	  directories with the same member count, segment positions, hard-link
69	  sharing layout and bit-for-bit state, staging each member like a fork
70	  (segment links first, the head pointer last) so a member appears as
71	  one complete chain or not at all; a killed import is resumed by
72	  re-running it and its debris is reclaimed by the next family
73	  operation.  Neither direction advances any member's optimizer step,
74	  and exporting the same family twice produces identical artifacts.
75	
76	Full snapshot wire format (all integers little-endian)::
77	
78	    magic        8 bytes  b"SEQECKP1"
79	    version      uint32   format version (3; versions 1 and 2 are read and
80	                          migrated, missing optimizer state starts at t=0
81	                          with zero moments)
82	    header_len   uint64   length of the JSON header in bytes

"""Checkpoint container: versioned binary snapshots for Sequential state.

A full snapshot fixes, in one self-describing document:

* every parameter tensor,
* every accumulated gradient (zeros when a parameter has none yet),
* the optimizer state (first and second moment per parameter plus the
  step count; zeros and ``t = 0`` when ``adam_step`` has never run),
* the slice-boundary hidden state of the latest boundary,
* the layer order and per-layer parameter shapes,
* the format version.

Two on-disk shapes share the same leaf encoding and trailer:

* **Full snapshots** (magic ``SEQECKP1``) -- one self-contained file, the
  format produced for file paths and in-memory buffers.
* **Incremental chains** -- a directory holding one full *basis* segment
  (``seg-00000000.seqd``) followed by delta segments that only encode the
  tensors that changed.  A small ``head`` pointer names the newest
  committed segment, so a crash between the segment write and the pointer
  update always recovers the previous complete state.  A chain can be
  **compacted** in place by a streaming online fold: the new basis is
  checked and written segment by segment, the tail deltas are converted a
  segment at a time in slots the chain already owned (so peak disk usage
  stays within the original chain plus the one new basis), and saves and
  loads interleave the whole time.  A marker plus a cross-process lease
  name a fold in progress, with the tail promoted and the head advanced
  in one final step, so a crash mid-compaction is rolled forward on the
  next open and the directory always holds exactly one complete chain --
  the old head's or the new head's.  A chain directory can also be
  **verified** strictly read-only: each segment is walked like a load and
  the first bad one is located and reported without a single write.
* **Chain families** -- a chain can be **forked** at any committed
  segment: the new chain directory shares every segment up to and
  including the fork point with the source chain (the prefix files are
  hard-linked, so they are stored once) and from then on maintains only
  its own head and the deltas it appends.  The chains of a family save,
  load, stream-compact and verify independently; shared segments are
  immutable (every write anywhere is a temp file plus a rename), and a
  shared segment's bytes are reclaimed by reachability -- exactly when no
  chain's head can reach it any more, whether the reference went away
  through a compaction or through the **deletion** of a whole branch.
  Reclamation is a pure reachability function, so sweeping again changes
  nothing; segments no head can reach (orphans left by a hard kill) and
  staging directories from a killed fork, delete or compaction are swept
  deterministically on the next fork, compaction, deletion or merge.  A
  family of chains can also be compacted in one call --
  :func:`compact_family` folds the prefix segments every member reaches
  through the same underlying files into one new basis segment shared by
  every member, with each member's own tail following it -- and verified
  read-only, with the first bad segment reported together with every
  chain that reaches it.
* **Branch merges** -- one chain's current state can be merged onto
  another: the target keeps every segment it had and receives one new,
  target-owned delta segment after its head carrying only the tensors in
  which the source's head state genuinely differs (an empty delta when
  the states already agree), so loading the target is bit for bit the
  source's merge-time state while the source's head and files never move
  and shared segments are never written twice.  The merge uses the same
  segment-then-head append commit a save does -- a kill leaves only the
  old or the new head, both one complete chain -- and its orphan residue
  is reclaimed by the next fork, compaction, deletion or merge.
* **Family export / import** -- a whole chain family packs into one
  self-contained artifact file (magic ``SEQFAMX1``): every shared
  segment is stored once as a deduplicated block and a manifest records
  the member order, each member's head and the block filling each of
  its segment positions.  Import restores the artifact into chain
  directories with the same member count, segment positions, hard-link
  sharing layout and bit-for-bit state, staging each member like a fork
  (segment links first, the head pointer last) so a member appears as
  one complete chain or not at all; a killed import is resumed by
  re-running it and its debris is reclaimed by the next family
  operation.  Neither direction advances any member's optimizer step,
  and exporting the same family twice produces identical artifacts.

Full snapshot wire format (all integers little-endian)::

    magic        8 bytes  b"SEQECKP1"
    version      uint32   format version (3; versions 1 and 2 are read and
                          migrated, missing optimizer state starts at t=0
                          with zero moments)
    header_len   uint64   length of the JSON header in bytes
    header       header_len bytes of UTF-8 JSON (shapes, layer order, flags)
    payload      one leaf per tensor element, each a 1-byte tag
                 ("i" | "f") followed by int64 or float64
    end_magic    12 bytes b"SEQECKP1END"
    leaf_count   uint64   number of encoded leaves
    payload_crc  uint32   CRC-32 of the header bytes followed by the payload

Delta segments use magic ``SEQDELTA`` / ``SEQDELTAEND`` with the same
framing; their header names the basis file, the segment number, the
hidden-slot count (or null) and the changed tensors as ``{"i", "s"}``
records, where *i* is the flat tensor index (params, then grads, then the
optimizer first moments, second moments and step count, then hidden
slots).  Delta segments written by the previous format version (2), whose
flat space ends after the hidden slots, are read and migrated as well.

Float leaves are emitted as raw IEEE-754 bytes, so values (including the
sign of negative zero) round-trip bit for bit.  Non-finite floats and
integers that do not fit in int64 are refused up front, and payloads that
merely *contain* such bit patterns are rejected on load as well.

Loading validates the whole document before anything is handed back:
truncation, corruption, a version that cannot be migrated, a missing or
unexpected field, or any structural problem rejects the entire checkpoint
with ValueError; nothing is silently filled in.
"""

_FAMILY_LOCK_NAME = ".seqfam.lock"

17	# Adam coefficients are fixed by the engine; callers only choose the rate.
18	_ADAM_BETA1 = 0.9
19	_ADAM_BETA2 = 0.999
20	_ADAM_EPSILON = 1e-8
21	
22	
23	def _zeros(shape):
24	    if not shape:
25	        return 0.0
26	    return [_zeros(shape[1:]) for _ in range(shape[0])]

29	def _parameters_fingerprint(params):
30	    """A deterministic bitwise fingerprint of every parameter's values."""
31	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
32	    for param in params:
33	        for dim in param.shape:
34	            digest.update(struct.pack("<q", dim))
35	        _fingerprint_tree(param._values(), digest)
36	    return digest.digest()
37	
38	
39	def _fingerprint_tree(value, digest):
40	    if isinstance(value, list):
41	        digest.update(b"[")
42	        for item in value:
43	            _fingerprint_tree(item, digest)
44	        digest.update(b"]")
45	    elif isinstance(value, bool):
46	        digest.update(b"?")
47	    elif isinstance(value, int):
48	        digest.update(b"i")
49	        digest.update(str(value).encode("ascii"))
50	        digest.update(b";")
51	    else:
52	        digest.update(b"f")
53	        digest.update(struct.pack("<d", value))
54

56	def _adam_update_trees(theta, m, v, grad, lr, m_correction, v_correction):
57	    """One Adam step on matching trees; returns ``(theta, m, v)`` updated.
58	
59	    The arithmetic order is fixed -- m and v first, then the bias
60	    corrections, then the parameter -- so a resumed run is bitwise
61	    identical to an uninterrupted one.
62	    """
63	    if isinstance(theta, list):
64	        new_theta, new_m, new_v = [], [], []
65	        for t_item, m_item, v_item, g_item in zip(theta, m, v, grad):
66	            nt, nm, nv = _adam_update_trees(
67	                t_item, m_item, v_item, g_item, lr, m_correction, v_correction
68	            )
69	            new_theta.append(nt)
70	            new_m.append(nm)
71	            new_v.append(nv)
72	        return new_theta, new_m, new_v
73	    m_next = _ADAM_BETA1 * m + 0.1 * grad
74	    v_next = _ADAM_BETA2 * v + 0.001 * (grad * grad)
75	    m_hat = m_next / m_correction
76	    v_hat = v_next / v_correction
77	    return theta - lr * m_hat / (math.sqrt(v_hat) + _ADAM_EPSILON), m_next, v_next

82	    if kind is None:

84	    if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
85	        raise ValueError("layer checkpoint_kind must be a non-empty string")

89	class Sequential:
90	    """Chains caller-provided layers in registration order.
91	
92	    Each layer must provide ``forward``, ``backward`` and ``parameters``.
93	    ``forward(batch, hidden=None)`` runs the batch through every layer in
94	    order; each layer consumes the previous layer's output plus its own
95	    hidden-state slot (``None`` when no hidden state is supplied, meaning
96	    the layer restarts from zeros) and returns an ``(output, hidden_slot)``
97	    pair. The slots stack in registration order into the chain's hidden
98	    state.
99	
100	    The engine keeps no gradient history across ``forward`` calls: hidden
101	    states carry values only, so a backward pass on a later segment can
102	    never add gradients to an earlier one. ``backward(loss)`` starts from
103	    the caller-computed scalar loss and walks the layers in reverse order,
104	    each layer passing the upstream gradient back and accumulating
105	    parameter gradients on its own tensors.
106	
107	    Besides the forward/backward cycle the container offers:
108	
109	    * ``update(learning_rate)`` -- one in-place gradient step
110	      ``theta <- theta - lr * grad`` on every parameter; gradients are
111	      not cleared (``zero_grad`` still does that).
112	    * ``adam_step(learning_rate)`` -- one in-place Adam step with the
113	      engine's fixed coefficients; the first/second moments and the step
114	      count ride along in every checkpoint.
115	    * ``set_recompute(enabled)`` -- bounded-memory mode: a segment keeps
116	      only its boundary hidden state plus a few anchors, and the backward
117	      pass recomputes the activations from them.
118	    * ``save(target)`` / ``load(source)`` -- atomic, versioned snapshots of
119	      parameters, accumulated gradients, optimizer state and
120	      slice-boundary hidden state, to a filesystem path, an
121	      incremental-chain directory or to an in-memory ``bytearray``.
122	    * ``compact(target, up_to=None)`` -- folds one incremental chain's
123	      basis and a prefix of its deltas into one new basis segment,
124	      crash-safely; the reassembled state is bit for bit unchanged.  With
125	      a list of chain directories (or ``MemoryChain`` stores) it
126	      performs one family-level fold: the prefix shared by every member
127	      becomes a single new basis segment shared by them all and each
128	      member's own tail follows it.
129	    * ``fork(source, target, up_to=None)`` -- derives a branch chain
130	      sharing the source chain's segments up to the fork point; each
131	      chain then maintains only its own head and appended deltas, and
132	      shared segments are reclaimed exactly when no chain can reach
133	      them any more.
134	    * ``delete(target)`` -- deletes one branch chain of a family: its
135	      directory, its head and the segments it alone owned.  Shared
136	      segments stay while any chain's head can reach them, and crash
137	      residue (staging directories, unreachable orphan segments) is
138	      swept deterministically.
139	    * ``merge(source, target)`` -- lands one chain's current state onto
140	      another chain by appending exactly one delta segment to the
141	      target; the target reassembles afterwards to the source's state
142	      bit for bit while the source is untouched and shared segments are
143	      never stored twice.
144	    * ``export_family(members, target)`` / ``import_family(source,
145	      target)`` -- pack a whole chain family into one self-contained
146	      artifact (shared segments stored once, every member's head and
147	      tail positions preserved) and restore it back into chain
148	      directories with the same member count, segment positions, shared
149	      layout and bit-for-bit state; both directions are crash-safe and
150	      advance no member's optimizer step.
151	
152	    All public operations are serialised by one re-entrant lock, so
153	    several threads may interleave ``forward``, ``backward``, ``update``,
154	    ``save`` and ``load`` calls: every observed parameter state is one a
155	    serial execution of the same calls could have produced, ``update`` is
156	    atomic and a snapshot always corresponds to one complete slice
157	    boundary -- never two passes half mixed.
158	    """
159	
160	    def __init__(self, modules):
161	        if isinstance(modules, (str, bytes)):
162	            raise ValueError("Sequential expects a non-empty sequence of layers")
163	        try:
164	            modules = list(modules)
165	        except TypeError:
166	            raise ValueError(
167	                "Sequential expects a non-empty sequence of layers"
168	            ) from None
169	        if len(modules) == 0:
170	            raise ValueError("Sequential requires at least one layer")
171	        for index, module in enumerate(modules):
172	            missing = [
173	                name
174	                for name in _REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES
175	                if not callable(getattr(module, name, None))
176	            ]
177	            if missing:
178	                raise ValueError(
179	                    f"layer at index {index} is missing required "
180	                    f"capabilit{'ies' if len(missing) > 1 else 'y'}: "
181	                    + ", ".join(missing)
182	                )
183	        self._modules = modules
184	        self._pending_backward = False
185	        self._hidden_shapes = None
186	        self._last_output = None
187	        self._last_hidden = None
188	        # Recompute mode: the configured switch plus the per-segment latch
189	        # with its anchors (segment input + incoming hidden values) and the
190	        # parameter fingerprint taken at forward time.
191	        self._recompute = False
192	        self._segment_recompute = False
193	        self._anchors = None
194	        self._forward_fingerprint = None
195	        # Retry anchors (segment input + incoming hidden values) kept in
196	        # every mode while a backward is pending: if a layer raises
197	        # mid-backward the segment's forward is replayed from them, so
198	        # layer caches a failed pass destroyed are rebuilt before the
199	        # caller retries.
200	        self._retry_anchors = None
201	        # Optimizer state: first/second moment trees per parameter plus the
202	        # step count.  Lazily sized to the parameter list on first use.
203	        self._adam_t = 0
204	        self._adam_m = None
205	        self._adam_v = None
206	        # Version a checkpoint was loaded from (None until the first load).
207	        self._loaded_from_version = None
208	        self._lock = threading.RLock()

210	    @property
211	    def loaded_from_version(self):
212	        """Format version the last ``load`` migrated from (``None`` before).
213	
214	        A version-1 or version-2 checkpoint reports ``1``/``2``; a native
215	        version-3 file reports ``3``. The source version is only updated on
216	        a successful load -- a checkpoint rejected mid-migration leaves the
217	        previous value untouched.
218	        """
219	        return self._loaded_from_version
